inspiration: Respawn-choice death screen: on death the window shows respawn locations and an auto-respawn timer, and a killer line updates live (DeathWindow.OnPlayerDeath takes an auto-respawn time; OnKillerUpdated refreshes the killer). Fit for death and respawn presentation (row 17): a loss that stays readable and bearable. Reference: interface/default/ea_deathwindow/source/deathwindow.lua lines 83 and 122.

Screen flash driven by hit-point changes, with an on/off gate (ScreenFlashWindow.OnPlayerHitPointsUpdated and SetEnabled/IsEnabled). Reads as impact without blocking the view, and the player can turn it off. Fit for hud-ui accessibility and combat feedback (row 10). Reference: interface/default/ea_screenflashwindow/source/screenflashwindow.lua lines 80 and 102.

Choose-one loot window: hovering an item row shows its item tooltip (EA_Window_ChooseOneLoot.OnMouseOverItem; the pick action itself was not read). Fit for the loot drop ceremony (row 18): a short row where inspecting comes before choosing. Reference: interface/default/ea_lootwindow/source/chooseonelootwindow.lua line 60.

Bestiary card as catalogue data: each creature row has an ID, subtype, image reference, armour class, and up to ten type/id pairs (interface/interfacecore/tome/bestiary/species.csv line 1). Fit for catalogue fields (row 21): a card built from data rows, not hand-written text.

Window-per-system layout: each window is a separate module with its own Lua and XML, and an action-bar cluster manager and a layout editor let the player move bars (ea_actionbars, easystem_layouteditor). Fit for hud-ui: player-editable HUD layout on a phone-sized screen.
Minimap and map windows: an overhead map window and a world map window are separate modules (ea_overheadmapwindow, ea_worldmapwindow, ea_zonecontrolwindow). Fit for the minimap topic (hud-ui).
Cast and target readouts: a cast-timer window, a mouse-over target window and an objective tracker are separate small windows. Fit for threat and target readability (hud-ui, row 14).

briefs.label: Respawn-choice death card
briefs.why: A death that offers a clear next step and a timer is less punishing than a blank screen. The card is readable at 375 wide because it is short.
briefs.keep: Respawn options listed on death, an auto-respawn timer, and a killer line that updates while the card is open.
briefs.change: Use three abstract respawn choices (nearest shrine, last camp, here) with no place names; a timer ring instead of a text counter. Keep Dom's rule: distinct original, not the donor's layout or text.

briefs.label: Hit flash with an off switch
briefs.why: A hit read on screen helps players who miss the health bar, and a switch keeps it kind to players who find flashing unpleasant.
briefs.keep: Flash driven by hit-point changes; an enable gate the player can flip.
briefs.change: A rim vignette in a threat colour rather than a full-screen tint; a setting that also softens the flash length. Keep Dom's rule: our own effect, not the donor's flash.

briefs.label: Choose-one loot row
briefs.why: A short row of rewards, where the player inspects before choosing, makes a loot drop feel like a decision.
briefs.keep: Hover or tap to inspect, then take one; the rest are left behind.
briefs.change: Three cards in a row at 375 wide with a rarity colour bar and a short sound on pick; a different ceremony (a lid lift). Keep Dom's rule: recreate as our own.

briefs.label: Bestiary silhouette card
briefs.why: A catalogue card with a silhouette and a short trait line makes a creature learnable before the fight.
briefs.keep: Each creature is a data row with an image, an armour value and a short list of type/id pairs; the card is built from the row.
briefs.change: Use three traits, a silhouette tile and a threat rating, not the donor's numeric fields; generate the card from our own catalogue (row 21). Keep Dom's rule: our own creatures and text.
